english: Let $P$ and $Q$ be the points of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{48}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$ with eccentric angles $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, respectively. Let $R$ be a point on the ellipse. Then the maximum value of the area of the triangle $PQR$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{48}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$ के बिन्दु $P$ तथा $Q$ के उत्केन्द्र कोण क्रमशः $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ तथा $-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ हैं। माना $R$ दीर्घवृत्त पर एक बिन्दु है। तब त्रिभुज $PQR$ के क्षेत्रफल का अधिकतम मान ______ है।
solution_full: The chord joining the points with eccentric angles $\alpha,\beta$ is $\dfrac{x}{a}\cos\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}+\dfrac{y}{b}\sin\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=\cos\dfrac{\alpha-\beta}{2}$. With $\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\dfrac{\alpha-\beta}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$: $\dfrac{x}{4\sqrt3}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+\dfrac{y}{4}\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac12$, i.e. $x+y=4$.
For $R(4\sqrt3\cos t,4\sin t)$, the distance from $x+y=4$ is $\dfrac{|4\sqrt3\cos t+4\sin t-4|}{\sqrt2}=\dfrac{|8\cos(t-\frac{\pi}{6})-4|}{\sqrt2}$.

Since $8\cos(t-\frac{\pi}{6})-4\in[-12,4]$, the largest distance is $\dfrac{12}{\sqrt2}=6\sqrt2$, at $t-\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\pi$, i.e. $t=\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$, $R(-6,-2)$ (the tangent there is parallel to $PQ$, on the far side).
Maximum area $=\dfrac12\cdot PQ\cdot6\sqrt2=\dfrac12\cdot6\sqrt2\cdot6\sqrt2=36$. (The point $t=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ on the near arc gives only $\dfrac12\cdot6\sqrt2\cdot2\sqrt2=12$.)
originality_note: New: the base chord is given only by eccentric angles, so its equation comes from the chord formula, and the far-side tangent point must be chosen over the near-side one (way 5). Closest known: maximum area of a triangle inscribed in an ellipse on a fixed chord. Different because: the near-arc point t = (alpha + beta)/2 that some books quote gives the wrong answer here (12), so the student must compare both arcs.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that both arcs are compared (12 versus 36) and the maximum is attained; numerical check over 200000 points. Changed: No change.
key_step: Chord PQ is x + y = 4; maximise the distance |8 cos(t - pi/6) - 4|/sqrt2, attained on the far arc.
justification: Routine chain: points from eccentric angles, chord equation, distance from a line and a trigonometric range; the far-arc check is the only trap. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q18 (L2), a routine ellipse extremum.

concept_use.Chord of a Ellipse: The chord joining eccentric angles pi/2 and -pi/6 is written from the chord formula as x + y = 4, and its length 6 sqrt2 is the base of the triangle.
